name: STAVE
expansion: Small-sample Tests of ABCD Variants and Estimators

intro.problem: The ABCD method estimates background in a signal region from three control regions, but it only works if the two discriminants are independent for background, and in a small-sample detector region both that independence and the statistical test used to check it become fragile.
intro.value: A background method validated for low-statistics regions would extend data-driven estimation to regions that may hold real sensitivity, and would separate a closure test that passes on merit from one that passes only because its error bars are too wide to fail.
intro.approach: We re-establish clean baselines, then test variants one at a time: decorrelation-penalty sweeps, closure-aware loss terms, kernel models of the joint background, and pretraining on a higher-statistics region transferred to the small one.
intro.goals: The outcome is a reproducible baseline and a ranked set of estimator variants scored on closure with honest uncertainties, ending in a recommendation for which estimators hold up in small samples and which do not.

questions: Does a closure test in a small sample carry real evidence, or do wide error bars simply absorb a same-size error?
Can what a model learns in a high-statistics region transfer to a low-statistics one without importing that region's biases?
Which estimator choice (penalty, kernel, or pretraining) moves closure, and what does each cost in discrimination?

timeline.label: Literature review of how barrel and endcap are handled in ABCD and LLP searches
Kernel-method ideas raised and first barrel plan outlined
Project named STAVE; ideas deck finished, with re-running the baseline as step one
Baseline re-run graded with a pre-registered evaluation framework
Compare closure-term loss variants on a replicated grid
Test a kernel classifier against the neural-network baseline
Test pretraining on the larger region and transferring to the smaller one
Plan a kernel-based model of the joint background
